issues.description: The template's Stock class calls StockIngredient.getQuantity(), but the template StockIngredient class defines retrieveQuantity() instead of getQuantity(). This method-name/signature mismatch causes compilation errors and contradicts the problem requirement to add standard getters for private fields. The solution repository uses getQuantity(), which aligns with Stock. Students will be blocked by this inconsistency.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename retrieveQuantity() in the template StockIngredient class to getQuantity(), or add a getQuantity() method that delegates to retrieveQuantity(), so that Stock can call getQuantity() as intended. Ensure all private fields have standard getter names (getName, getPrice, getQuantity) to match the problem statement and the solution implementation.

issues.description: The template defines a StockIngredient getter named retrieveQuantity(), while the rest of the code and the solution expect/get use getQuantity(). The problem statement also instructs students to add getters for private fields (implying standard getX naming). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual getter (ingredient quantity) will confuse students and causes a mismatch between classes (Stock calls getQuantity()) and the StockIngredient API provided in the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template getter retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() (and keep the existing setQuantity/getName/getPrice names). Ensure all usages (e.g., in Stock.add and Stock.take) reference getQuantity(). This aligns the template, solution, and problem statement expectation for standard getter naming.
